components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Orange filled CTA button with a diagonal shimmer sweep on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { position: relative; overflow: hidden; background-color: #FB8500; color: #112250; font-family: 'Bricolage Grotesque', sans-serif; text-transform: uppercase; font-weight: 200; font-size: 1.25rem; letter-spacing: 0.08em; border-radius: 6px; padding: 13px 28px 14px; border: none; box-shadow: 0px 4px 17px 0px rgba(0,0,0,0.3); cursor: pointer; transition: all 500ms cubic-bezier(0.035, 0.625, 0, 1); } .ds-btn-primary::after { content: ''; position: absolute; top: 0; left: -80%; width: 50%; height: 100%; background: linear-gradient(90deg, transparent, rgba(255,255,255,0.22), transparent); transform: skewX(-15deg); pointer-events: none; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background-color: #112250; color: #fff; } .ds-btn-primary:hover::after { animation: ds-shimmer 0.55s ease forwards; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.97); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #003DDE; outline-offset: 2px; } @keyframes ds-shimmer { from { left: -80%; } to { left: 130%; } }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: White filled button, used against the orange CTABanner backdrop.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background-color: #FFFFFF; color: #003DDE; font-family: 'Bricolage Grotesque', sans-serif; text-transform: uppercase; font-weight: 200; font-size: 1.25rem; letter-spacing: 0.08em; border-radius: 6px; padding: 13px 28px 14px; border: none; box-shadow: 0px 4px 17px 0px rgba(0,0,0,0.3); cursor: pointer; transition: all 500ms cubic-bezier(0.035, 0.625, 0, 1); } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background-color: #112250; color: #fff; } .ds-btn-secondary:active { transform: scale(0.97); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #003DDE; outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.overview:
The site reads like a French institutional magazine, not a SaaS landing page: flat, saturated color fields (Bleu Roi, Vert Eau, Bleu Nuit) carry full-bleed reportage photography of real sites and real people, and every section title is set in a cold, thin, all-caps grotesque that is deliberately warmed by exactly one italic serif word per heading. That single italic word is the whole personality budget of the type system — it is never spent twice in the same title, and it is never used for body copy.

The palette itself is a doctrine, not a preference: Bleu Roi (#003DDE) and Vert Eau (#D2E6DC) were chosen and their contrast ratios engineered on purpose (documented inline in globals.css — accent 5.9:1 on ground, navy-on-orange 6.2:1 chosen deliberately over white's 2.5:1). Orange (#FB8500) is reserved for the single call-to-action gesture per view, and yellow (#FFE35B) appears only as a small warm counterpoint, never a field color. Nothing in the system is flat-and-shadowless: buttons, the fixed nav bar, and cards all carry a soft ambient drop-shadow that lifts them off the flat color ground.
keyCharacteristics: Flat, saturated color fields (never gradients as backgrounds — gradients exist only as photo-legibility overlays)
Full-bleed photography with a bottom-heavy Bleu Nuit gradient overlay for text legibility
Bricolage Grotesque thin/bold + DM Serif Display italic pairing, uppercase by default
One italic accent word per heading — the system's only ornament
Soft ambient drop-shadows on all interactive surfaces (buttons, nav, cards) — the system's only depth cue
The 6 A grid and the two named associates are recurring, non-negotiable structural motifs, not decoration

rules.name: The Engineered Contrast Rule
rules.body: Every text-on-color pairing in this system was chosen for a specific measured ratio, not for taste. Any new pairing must be checked against WCAG AA before shipping and commented inline.

rules.name: The Single Accent Rule
rules.body: Orange appears at most once per view as a filled surface. A second action uses .btn-blanc or .btn-bleu, never a second orange fill.

rules.name: The One Italic Word Rule
rules.body: DM Serif Display italic is reserved for exactly the accent portion of a composed heading or a 6 A title. Never upright, never in body copy, never twice in one heading.

rules.name: The Reserved Header Rule
rules.body: Any full-height or fixed-position content must account for --header-h and --cookie-banner-h in its own padding.

rules.name: The Ambient-Not-Structural Rule
rules.body: Shadows communicate 'this is a clickable/floating object,' not hierarchy or state depth. Present at rest, not only on hover.

rules.name: The Two-Radius Rule
rules.body: Hand-styled components (buttons, inputs, badges) use the 4-6px scale; Tailwind-authored components use Tailwind's own radius scale. Don't mix them.

dos: Do use AccentHeading for section titles instead of a raw h2/h3 — the bold-lead + italic-accent pairing is the house rule, not a one-off choice.
Do wrap new sections in Reveal for the scroll-in entrance, and trust its built-in prefers-reduced-motion fallback rather than adding a second one.
Do keep a soft ambient drop-shadow (0px 4px 17px 0px rgba(0,0,0,0.3-0.4)) on any new clickable button-like surface — flat/shadowless buttons break the system's one depth cue.
Do check and comment the contrast ratio inline (as globals.css already does) whenever pairing a new text color against a background.
Do keep photography full-color and full-bleed with a Bleu Nuit gradient overlay for legibility, never a flat color block standing in for a missing photo.
donts: Don't use DM Serif Display italic outside a heading's accent word or a 6 A title — never for body copy, never twice in one heading.
Don't introduce a fourth button variant or a new fill color for actions; the orange/white/navy trio already covers primary/secondary/tertiary.
Don't grayscale or desaturate partner/client logos — their brand color is the intended signal, not noise to normalize away.
Don't invent case-study numbers, client names, or testimonials to fill /realisations or /blog — every entry there today is confirmed placeholder.
Don't mix Tailwind's radius scale onto a hand-styled component or vice versa — see The Two-Radius Rule.
